business_problem: The district faced challenges with data compliance and privacy, especially with unstructured data from teachers.
solution_summary: School District No 43 Coquitlam, a Education organization in Canada, modernized this data lake / data warehouse modernization workload with Power Apps, Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft 365 A5, and Microsoft Purview. The district faced challenges with data compliance and privacy, especially with unstructured data from teachers. Power Apps delivers low-code applications tailored to frontline or business-process use cases. Power BI publishes dashboards and self-service analytics so business users can act on fresher insights. Microsoft Fabric unifies data engineering, storage, analytics, and BI on a shared data platform. Data from operational systems is ingested into Power Apps, processed across Power BI, and surfaced through Microsoft Fabric so teams can act on fresher operational insight. Applies automated information governance before broader AI adoption.

evidence_quotes: The district faced challenges with data compliance and privacy, especially with unstructured data from teachers.

Coquitlam’s transformation, powered by its partnership with Microsoft, has enabled the district to build a secure infrastructure to store raw and structured data, which Coquitlam uses to make informed, real-time decisions.
They chose to adopt a data platform infused with AI— including Power Apps, Power BI, and Microsoft Fabric—to make the most of their data while keeping it safe.

In the past, Coquitlam discovered that 80% of its data was unstructured, posing significant risks and potential compliance issues. Recognizing this, Whiffin’s team leveraged Microsoft’s framework to strategically balance in-house capabilities with outsourced maintenance and compliance.
